Lactuca watsoniana é uma espécie de plantas pertencente à família Asteraceae, endémica das ilhas dos Açores onde é conhecida pelo nome popular de alfacinha. Surge nas ilhas Terceira, São Miguel, São Jorge, Pico e Faial.

Erik Sjögren - Plantas e Flores dos Açores. Edição do autor 2001.
 {{Link||2=http://www.horta.uac.pt/species/plantae/Lactuca_watsoniana/Lactuca_watsoniana.htm |3=horta.uac.pt}}

It has been shown by Dias & al. (2018) that Lactuca watsoniana is sister to the North American allotetraploid L. canadensis group, with which it shares the same chromosome number and morphological features such as of the achenes. The SW European Alpine-Pyrenean L. plumieri was resolved as sister to the North American-Azorean clade.

Lactuca watsoniana occurs at elevations between 600 and 900 m, where it grows chiefly in open but somehow sheltered, wind-protected habitats, in particular on the steep slopes of craters, in deep narrow ravines and at the foot of rock faces. Its localities are characterised by permanent water supply or permanent moisture in combination with high relative humidity. The species is part of the association dominated by the tussock-forming Festuca jubata, which is particularly rich in endemic species (such as Tolpis azorica, Senecio malvifolius, Sanicula azorica, Holcus rigidus). This association is in close contact with and partly interpenetrated by the juniper fog woodlands (Sjögren 1973; Lüpnitz 1976).
Lactuca watsoniana is classified as Endangered (EN, B2ab (i, ii, iii); C2a(i)).

Perennial tall herb, to c. 180 cm with basal leaf rosette and strong taproot; lateral roots sometimes with root born shoots giving rise to daughter plants. Rosette leaves up to c. 60 cm long and c. (10-)14–18 cm wide, usually with a petiole or winged petiole up to 2/3 of the length of the entire leaf; lamina entire , ovate with cordate base and rounded to obtuse apex; margin coarsely and irregularly sinuate-dentate; upper leaf surface bright green, glabrous and shiny, lower surface pale to greyish green due to epicuticular waxes and with woolly hairs especially along the veins. Rosette axis shooting forth a single erect, leafy, green (when fresh), glabrous flowering stem, only branching apically and, perishing after fruiting. Lower cauline leaves sessile and sagittately clasping the stem, lamina ovate with subacute to acute tip, similar in size to the rosette leaves; higher up the stem leaves becoming obovate and continuously smaller, in the synflorescencse region reduced to lanceolate, clasping bracts. Synflorescence paniculiform with numerous capitula. Peduncles mostly c. 0.5-1 cm long, with bracts. Capitula with 5-13 flowers. Involucre at anthesis narrowly cylindrical, 1.5-5.5 mm in diameter, 9–14 mm long, not prolonged towards fruiting. Outer involucral bracts gradually longer centripetally, outermost narrowly ovate, acute, 1.5-4 mm long, 0.5-2 mm wide, innermost linear-lanceolate, up to c. 3/4 as long the inner ones; inner involucral bracts 5(-8), linear-lanceolate, acute, in one row. Corolloa white (when fresh), ligule 10–25 mm long, 3–6 mm wide, tube to 18 mm long; anther tube 1.6-6.8 mm long, blue (when fresh); style and style arms whitish (when fresh). Achenes 3.1-5.6 mm long including a stout beak of 1-1.4 mm, 0.7-2.4 mm wide, body strongly compressed with 2 lateral flat, wingg-like ribs and 1 weak narrow and sometimes faint medium rib on either face, broadly elliptical in outline, blackish and often mottled pale brown, surface with faint transversal wrinkles, carpopodium a small pale annulus; beak concolorous or sometimes paler. Pappus 4-7 mm long, of white, scabrid bristles with 2-3 cells in diameter near the base and all of the same size. [E. F. Dias & N. Kilian, 2016]\r\r
Lactuca watsoniana is known from five (Faial, Pico, São Miguel, Terceira and São Jorge) of the nine islands of the Azores archipelago, but has most likely gone extinct on São Jorge.

Lactuca watsoniana is tetraploid with 2n=34 chromosomes. It shares this number with the allotetraploid North American Lactuca species. , This number can be explained by a cross between progenitors with a basic chromosome number of x=8 and x=9.

The epithet watsoniana honours the British botanist Hewett Cottrell Watson (1804-1881), who essentially contributed to the knowledge of the botany of the Azores and noted a sterile large-leaved Compositae from the Caldeira of Fayal first in 1844 (London J. Bot. 8: 615), which Trelease assumed to be this species.
